title: Search code on GitHub in the browser
summary: This post explains two browser-based methods for searching Business Central code on GitHub: using GitHub's native code search for quick keyword queries across repositories, and using github.dev editor to perform VS Code-style searches on any branch including historical code repositories.
key_points: GitHub code search is fast and requires no local setup, but only searches the default branch of repositories
github.dev editor provides VS Code search capabilities in the browser for any branch, useful for accessing historical code repositories like Stefan Maron's Code History repos
Browser-based searching avoids cluttering your machine and eliminates the need to pull and refresh local repositories
Code search is limited to keyword matching; symbol-based analysis like 'Find references' still requires local VS Code with downloaded symbols

quotes.text: The browser search is much faster than to open and load a large repository before you can even enter your search criteria.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains the key advantage of browser-based searching for development efficiency
